name: NASA 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
what_it_contains: Comprehensive breakdown of the five primary spaceflight hazards: Space Radiation, Isolation and Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields (microgravity), and Hostile/Closed Environments.

name: NASA Risks of Human Spaceflight
what_it_contains: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports detailing operational risks: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Conditions, Psychiatric Disorders, Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, Workload, and Fatigue.

name: NASA Ongoing HRP Research in Space
what_it_contains: Active biomedical and behavioral research projects aboard the International Space Station, cognitive assessment batteries, behavioral countermeasures, and autonomic physiological tracking.

name: CSA: Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
what_it_contains: Canadian Space Agency technologies and research on measuring radiation exposure in space, bubble detectors, active neutron spectrometers, and monitoring astronaut health over long-duration missions.

name: CSA: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
what_it_contains: Exploration of the unique microgravity space environment, physiological adaptations (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, neurovestibular), psychological isolation, and medical countermeasures.

name: NASA Space Apps 2026: Health Monitoring Software Challenge Introduction Video
what_it_contains: Official NASA challenge introductory briefing detailing requirements for visual health assessment tools, self-monitoring software, multi-system integration, and clinical early warning principles.
